original_metadata.title: For every real nu>-1, the infinite complex inverse-Wishart measure has an ergodic decomposition with zero Gaussian component, finite trace equal to the sum of positive spectral parameters, and the inverted Bessel determinantal spectrum
original_metadata.author: Theodoros Assiotis
original_metadata.source_title: Ergodic Decomposition for Inverse Wishart Measures on Infinite Positive-Definite Matrices
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The hard-edge kernel limit alone determines only visible eigenvalues and can leave hidden trace mass or a Gaussian component in the ergodic parameters. The author proves uniform small-particle moment control across all nu>-1, then combines it with positivity and a Fatou argument to identify the trace and eliminate both residual components. This resolves the full ergodic decomposition of an infinite-dimensional matrix measure rather than just a finite-dimensional spectral limit.

proof_review.note: The complete main Theorem1.6 proof chain was read: inverse-Wishart consistency via Bessel-polynomial backward shift and matrix corners (Section2), hard-edge Laguerre/Bessel identification (Section4), all three parameter ranges of the uniform small-particle first-moment estimate (Section5), the vanishing Gaussian parameter (Section6), and the new positivity/Fatou argument identifying the finite trace parameter with the sum of asymptotic eigenvalues (Section7). The existing ergodic-method classification and hard-edge convergence are credited background. The new uniform integrability and absence of hidden trace mass are supplied, including the negative-nu case; merely identifying the limiting point process would not suffice. Bounded low-degree notation details are recorded explicitly in the warning; no independent new theorem proof is generated.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem1.6 for every real nu>-1. M^(nu) is the projective probability measure on infinite positive-definite complex Hermitian matrices whose N-corner density is the normalized det(X)^(-nu-2N)*exp(-2*Tr(X^-1)) on H^+(N). In the Pickrell–Olshanski–Vershik parametrization, its spectral measure is supported on Omega_0^+: every negative alpha vanishes, all positive alpha_i are nonzero, gamma_2=0, and gamma_1=sum_i alpha_i^+<infinity. The positive parameters form the determinantal process on (0,infinity) with Lebesgue kernel K_infty^nu(x,y)=8/(x*y)*J_nu(8/x,8/y), where J_nu is the exact Bessel kernel of Definition1.5. No infinite-mass inverse-Wishart parameter range, real-matrix analogue or Hua–Pickrell trace result is asserted.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: In Section5 the displayed split of the Laguerre polynomial sum starts at positive degree although its preceding kernel definition starts at degree zero; the preceding normalized-wavefunction tail estimate also controls that single degree-zero term. This is a bounded routine endpoint detail, not a replacement for the supplied uniform bulk estimate. In the nu=0 auxiliary bound the text prints -l*log(l)-l for an integral whose endpoint term has the opposite sign; the subsequently chosen l=o(epsilon) preserves the stated qualitative smallness. The raw published proof is reproduced unchanged and these editorial observations are separate from the author text.
